capture.final_message:
Prove all four component propositions independently, then assemble each equivalence using “true iff true.”

- The group-theoretic statement is the defining first step of the upper central series:
  \[
  Z_1(G)=Z(G).
  \]

- The infinitude statement is Dirichlet’s theorem on primes in arithmetic progressions, applied to \(a\) modulo the nonzero modulus \(q\), using `Nat.Coprime a q`.

- For the cyclotomic statement, express
  \[
  N_{L/K}(\zeta_p-1)
  \]
  through the minimal polynomial \(\Phi_p\). Irreducibility identifies the conjugates, so the norm is \((-1)^{p-1}\Phi_p(1)\). Since \(p\) is prime, \(\Phi_p(1)=p\); the assumption \(p\ne2\) makes \(p-1\) even and removes the sign.

- Rewrite the real series using
  \[
  \sin(\pi n/2)=
  \begin{cases}
  0,&n\text{ even},\\
  (-1)^k,&n=2k+1.
  \end{cases}
  \]
  It becomes the Dirichlet beta value
  \[
  \sum_{k\ge0}\frac{(-1)^k}{(2k+1)^3}
  =\beta(3)=\frac{\pi^3}{32}.
  \]
  Absolute convergence upgrades the ordinary `HasSum` result to the requested unconditional summation filter.

Finally combine the two proven sides of each `Iff`, and then form the outer conjunction.
